hints: Look at the vertical size on the c.r.o. screen and count divisions from the middle of the sine wave to the top of a peak.
Recall that Y-gain of $2 \text{ V div}^{-1}$ means each vertical division equals $2 \text{ V}$, while amplitude is centre-to-peak not trough-to-peak.
Ignore the $50 \text{ ms div}^{-1}$ time-base setting because it controls the horizontal time scale, not the vertical voltage.
walkthrough: Identify the vertical deflection that gives amplitude: the distance from the equilibrium centre line to the maximum of the sine wave on the trace.
From the grid the peak is $1$ division above the centre and the trough is $1$ division below the centre, so the amplitude height is $1$ div.
State the rule for vertical voltage: $V = \text{number of vertical divisions} \times \text{Y-gain}$.
Substitute the values with units: $V = 1 \text{ div} \times 2 \text{ V div}^{-1} = 2 \text{ V}$.
Check that the $50 \text{ ms div}^{-1}$ time-base is not needed because amplitude is a voltage, and the peak-to-peak value would be $4 \text{ V}$. This is option A.

options.A: Peak height is $1$ div and $1 \times 2 \text{ V div}^{-1} = 2 \text{ V}$, which is the amplitude.
options.B: This is the peak-to-peak voltage of $2$ div, not the amplitude measured from the centre to the peak.
options.C: This confuses the vertical scale with another count and does not equal $1 \text{ div} \times 2 \text{ V div}^{-1}$.
options.D: This uses the $50 \text{ ms div}^{-1}$ time-base or a $5$ div width, which controls time not vertical voltage.
